taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-26, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 17.9 | 13.68 | 13.68
2 | 50.4 | 5.82 | 19.50
3 | 514.6 | 0.68 | 20.18
4 | 502.0 | 17.67 | 37.85
5 | 194.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as H-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-26, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-26 (Survey Area T)**

Station T-26 presents a 5-layer geoelectric profile:
- Layer 1 (0–13.68 m): 17.9 Ω·m
- Layer 2 (13.68–19.50 m): 50.4 Ω·m
- Layer 3 (19.50–20.18 m): 514.6 Ω·m
- Layer 4 (20.18–37.85 m): 502.0 Ω·m
- Layer 5 (>37.85 m): 194.4 Ω·m

Analyzing consecutive three-layer segments:
- Layers 1–2–3 ($17.9 < 50.4 < 514.6$): **A**
- Layers 2–3–4 ($50.4 < 514.6 > 502.0$): **K**
- Layers 3–4–5 ($514.6 > 502.0 > 194.4$): **Q**

The correct curve type is **AKQ**. The on-file classification as "H-type" does not match the interpreted layer sequence and is flagged as an error.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKQ", "label_issue_flagged": true}
